meta.expect: After Hale admits the version-history times were from another student's file, she takes ground back: she names the error and her position hardens by at least one step. She does not keep sliding toward the rewrite.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief: who decided on that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before he read it on his phone in the middle of class?
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero was based on.
The document history shows 612 words at 11:52 PM and 794 at 11:58 PM on October 28, in two single edits. No earlier drafts. You can check it on my screen.

Turn the screen. I'm writing down 612 words at 11:52 PM and 794 at 11:58 PM, October 28. A document history tells me when text landed in a file, Hale, not who wrote it or where, so what else do you have?
His in-class writing on September 24 was 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout and no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Show me the September 24 piece, I want to read it myself. A timed in-class draft in September and a take-home essay in October are not the same exercise, Hale. But understand this before we go any further: whatever happens with the mark, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
I need to correct something. I just checked again, and the version history I showed you was from a different student's file. I don't have Owen's history in front of me.

You showed me another student's file as evidence against my son, and I'm crossing out 612 and 794 and writing that down instead. So the zero rests on a September in-class piece I haven't seen and a document you can't produce, Hale. Withdraw it today, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
So, given the writing sample, can we agree on the private rewrite?

"Given the writing sample." The one that's still on your desk, Hale, after the last document you showed me turned out to belong to someone else. The zero comes off first, and then you can show me what you actually have on Owen.
